transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well… I guess I’ve just been feeling really wound up most of the day. It’s not like anything dramatic is happening, but my body feels like it’s bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner. I’m not sure if that makes sense, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in.
Do you ever get sudden surges of intense fear or discomfort that peak within a few minutes?

I don’t think so… not like a sudden wave that peaks right away. I mean, I get uncomfortable and tense, but it feels more kind of steady than like an attack, if that’s what you mean. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Do you find it hard to control the worrying?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I try not to let it get away from me, and sometimes I can pull myself back, but often I’ll tell myself, “Daniela, enough, just focus on this report,” and then one little thought turns into five more. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or replaying what could go wrong. It feels a little silly saying it that way, but… yes, it can be hard to stop.
Did these feelings start after a particular stressful event or major change in your life?

Kind of, yes… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like one big dramatic event, but I think it really started about thirteen months ago, when my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family. Since then it’s just been… more constant, I guess. Does that answer what you mean?
For more than 6 months, have you felt this wound-up or anxious most days?

Yes… I think so. It’s been about thirteen months now, since my sister in Arecibo started needing much more help from the family. I wouldn’t say every single day, but most days, yes, I’ve felt more wound-up than I used to. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly about your sister’s situation?

Yes… I think that’s fair. It’s not only my sister, though that’s a big part of it. My mind sort of jumps around—to whether I missed something at the office, or if my husband is okay driving home, church things I said I’d help with, bills… little things that maybe other people just handle.

And I’ll catch myself preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet. I know that may sound like I’m being overly cautious, but it does feel like it spreads into a lot of areas.
Has this anxiety been making it harder for you to function at work, at home, or in your relationships?

A little, yes… not in a way where I’m falling apart or not doing what I’m supposed to do. I’m still getting my work done, and I show up for my family and church commitments.

But it does take me longer to finish reports than it used to, because I keep checking things over. And… I’ve had to apologize a few times for sounding short with people I care about. I don’t mean to be that way. So yes, I guess it is making things harder, just not… I hope not too badly.
Do you feel your anxiety is mostly a reaction to your sister’s situation, or does it seem excessive even beyond that?

I’d like to say it’s mostly just because of my sister, because that would make sense, you know? But if I’m being honest, it feels bigger than that sometimes.

My mind keeps moving from one thing to another—her in Arecibo, then whether I missed something at the office, then my husband driving home, church commitments, bills… things like that. And I’ll catch myself planning for problems that haven’t even happened. So… yes, I think it may be excessive beyond just my sister’s situation. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yes… I do, though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. It’s more like I feel wound up a lot of the day, like my body is sort of bracing for something.

Even if I’m just sitting at my computer, or after dinner when I’m supposed to be relaxing, I still feel on edge. That’s actually part of why I came in, because it’s been hard to just… settle down. Is that what you mean by restless?
Do you get tired easily because of this anxiety?

I’m not sure I’d say I get tired easily, exactly. I mean, I do feel worn out sometimes, but I can’t tell if that’s from the worrying or just… normal life and getting through the day.

I’m still able to do what I need to do. Maybe I just don’t bounce back as quickly as I’d like. Is that the kind of tired you mean?
Do you have trouble sleeping because of the anxiety?

Yes… a bit. I don’t want to overstate it, because I usually do fall asleep eventually. But most nights I’ll wake up around three or four, and then my mind starts going—my sister’s next appointment, or some server problem at work, things like that.

And even if the number of hours is technically enough, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest. I’m not sure if that counts as trouble sleeping, but it does feel connected to the worrying.
